newsitem.title: USA: Ford introduces 2 new concepts vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Ford introduces 2 new concepts vehicles.

text.p: Ford Motor Co introduced two concepts vehicles Tuesday, a new coupe designed for more practicality and a high-performance sport/utility that executives said has a good chance of going into production.

The new vehicles, unveiled at the North American International Auto Show, are the Mercury MC4 and the Ford Tremor, a sport/utility based on the current Explorer that Ford said is aimed at people who want a more high-performance off-road vehicle.
Jacques Nasser, president of Ford's automotive operations, said a decision will be made on the Tremor soon, depending in part on the reaction it gets from the public.
"We'd love to do it. We think there's a marketplace for it," he said.

The Tremor has a a 4.6 liter, five-valve, dual overhead camshaft engine that generates 380 horsepower. It comes with independent rear suspension, all-wheel drive and features a more aggressive look than the Explorer.
Nasser described the MC4 as an "off-the-wall bookend" concept vehicle that Ford designers came up with to test more extreme versions of various ideas.
The car reflects the "new edge" design theme that combines smooth sculpted lines with crisp corners.

In addition to its two doors, the car also has a reverse door system on both sides to allow for easier access to the vehicle's back seat. The trunk features a "gull-wing" lid that opens from either side for more flexible loading.
Nasser did not offer a timetable whether the car would be built.
